title: Deliver Changes Reproducibly and Safely
objective: Manage configuration as code and operate the assessment of change impact, approvals, phased deployment, validation, and rollback.

prerequisites.title: Operate observation through remediation as one continuous process
Demonstrate Reliability and Business Continuity Through Operations

sections.title: Declare Configuration and Review Differences
paragraphs: Operations personnel who use CloudFormation describe resources and properties in templates and manage them as stacks. Manual changes made in the console can undermine consistency with the templates and reproducibility during recovery, so necessary changes are brought back into the code and review process.

Before making changes, verify the target account, Region, stack, dependent resources, and the impact of the update. Review the resources that will be created, updated, or deleted through change sets and similar mechanisms, and stop any unintended replacements or deletions before approval.

sections.title: Apply Changes in Small, Observable Steps
paragraphs: The release team applies the configuration change to a limited part of production and checks the predetermined latency, error rate, and business metrics. It expands the rollout only if the criteria for proceeding are met and no stop condition applies.

For gradual changes, make it possible to identify whether the old or new version processed each request. If an anomaly occurs, revert the configuration or deployment to a known-good state, record the cause, and then retry.

sections.title: Establishing Permission and Approval Boundaries for Automation
paragraphs: Automation authors minimize the resources that a runbook can modify and the permissions granted to its IAM role. They separate the roles of executor, approver, and auditor, and ensure that execution inputs, execution results, and reasons for failure can be recorded.

Even when automating repetitive remediation, define target selection, the concurrency limit, stopping on failure, and manual escalation. Automation does not eliminate responsibility for changes; it is a mechanism for consistently executing procedures that can be verified.

At the top of the diagram, a load balancer distributes user requests between stable and canary targets. Below, the release team reviews the infrastructure change set and deploys the new release only within the approved scope. The team measures user impact and expands the rollout if the criteria for proceeding are met and no stop condition applies. If a stop condition is reached, it restores a known-good state.

checkpoints.prompt: The person responsible for changing the route configuration of a production VPC with CloudFormation wants to avoid unintended deletions or replacements before approval. Select one most appropriate action to take before applying the change.

choices.text: Make the change in the console first and update the template afterward.
choices.explanation: This undermines configuration reproducibility and change tracking.

choices.text: Verify the target account, Region, stack, and dependent resources, then review the differences in a change set.
choices.explanation: You can review the creations, updates, and deletions caused by the change before applying it.

choices.text: Update all stacks at the same time without verifying which resources are targeted.
choices.explanation: You cannot control the scope of the impact.

checkpoints.prompt: A release owner is gradually applying application-configuration changes to production. Choose the single most appropriate criterion for deciding whether to proceed at each stage.

choices.text: Verify that predefined latency, error-rate, and business metrics meet the criteria for proceeding.
choices.explanation: This allows the rollout to be expanded based on the change's effects and its impact on users.

choices.text: Stop monitoring and immediately apply the change to all users.
choices.explanation: This prevents early detection of anomalies and delays rollback.

choices.text: Continue applying the change even during anomalies without identifying the post-change version.
choices.explanation: This makes it impossible to isolate the cause and roll back safely.

checkpoints.prompt: An operations team creating a Systems Manager Automation runbook wants to prevent changes to unintended targets. Choose one most appropriate runbook design.

choices.text: Define target selection, a least-privilege execution role, approvals, the maximum number of concurrent executions, stop conditions, and audit records.
choices.explanation: This makes it possible to verify the automation’s scope of action and accountability.

choices.text: Target all resources and execute without approval using administrator privileges.
choices.explanation: The scope of impact will be larger if an incorrect operation occurs.

choices.text: Do not record execution results, and automatically retry indefinitely even after a failure.
choices.explanation: This makes it impossible to identify problems and may expand the damage.
